### GAP-HR-LEAVE-APPLY-01  ·  HIGH  ·  partly  ·  theme WIRING

- [x] **Status** — PR #1731 (merged): new preview route reuses enforceCcsLeaveRules verbatim (same reads, no side effects); IDOR guard (self/manager-of-target/HR-role) proven by a live 403 in a real test run. W2 rescan: preview now answers rule outcomes as data (valid/violations/warnings/holidaysInRange/balance/balanceAfter) from the one evaluateLeaveRules path submit uses; the form shows the debit, the balance it leaves and engine notices (sandwich etc.), blocks Submit inline the moment the server reports a violation or refuses the preview, the misleading 'excludes weekends & holidays' copy is corrected (approximate = calendar days, offline only), and the success message names the server-confirmed days; real-DB tests cover a CL Fri-Mon holiday range and an EL range where the engine count (1) differs from the calendar count (4). (W2 hr rescan: completed by #PRNUM)
- **First-pass claim:** The 'Duration' shown and submitted is a calendar-day count including weekends and holidays (calcDays, ApplyLeaveForm.tsx), but the server recomputes days under CCS leave rules and debits that instead (leave/routes.ts:235-240 'BUG-1 fix'). The user is never shown the number actually debited, and the balance warning itself admits the count is 'approximate'.
- **Verified evidence:** calcDays (ApplyLeaveForm.tsx:142-148) returns inclusive calendar days and that value is posted as daysApplied (185-193) to /v1/hrms/leave-requests. The server recomputes via enforceCcsLeaveRules (routes.ts:243-249; rules-engine.ts:283-307: working days vs calendar days by countMethod, holidays, sandwich, prefix/suffix) and persists/debits computedDays; non-engine codes keep the client value. The POST returns only 202 {id,status,correlationId}, so the user never sees the debited number. Correction: the form does show a disclaimer (en.json:2713 'Approximate — excludes weekends & holidays.'), but it is wrong: calcDays does NOT exclude weekends/holidays, and balanceWarning (2712) says 'calendar days'. Contradictory copy makes the gap worse.
- **Files to change:** `services/hrms-service/src/modules/leave/routes.ts`, `services/hrms-service/src/modules/leave/rules-engine.ts`, `apps/web/src/app/(app)/hr/leave/apply/ApplyLeaveForm.tsx`, `apps/web/src/messages/en.json`, `apps/web/src/messages/hi.json`, `apps/web/src/messages/kn.json`, `apps/web/src/messages/ta.json`, `apps/web/src/messages/te.json`
- **Fix steps:**
  1. Backend: extract the validation part of enforceCcsLeaveRules into a function returning {computedDays, warnings, errors, holidaysInRange}; add a new read-only preview endpoint (e.g. POST /v1/hrms/leave-requests/preview, ALL_ROLES, same body minus reason, same IDOR guard) that calls it and returns the result without publishing.
  2. Web: in ApplyLeaveForm debounce a call to the preview when allocId/fromDate/toDate change (AbortController); render 'X days will be debited from <type>' plus rules-engine warnings (sandwich etc.) and the resulting balance.
  3. Disable Submit and show inline error when preview errors (insufficient balance, rule violation); fall back to the current approximate path only if preview fails.
  4. Delete calcDays as the source of truth and fix/remove calendarDaysDisclaimer and balanceWarning copy in all locales.
  5. Show the server-confirmed days on the success message/history (days from leave list).
- **Acceptance:**
  - API test: preview for CL Fri-Mon spanning a holiday returns the same computedDays that POST /leave-requests persists.
  - Component test: choosing dates shows the previewed debit, not the calendar count; a range that exceeds balance shows the 422 message and disables Submit.
  - Offline queued submissions (fetchOrQueue) still work and show the 'approximate' state.
- **Needs:** web+backend  ·  **Effort:** M ~1-2d  ·  **Risk:** Leave debit feeds balances and payroll LOP; preview and submit must share one code path or they will diverge; preview endpoint is another read that must apply the IDOR guard (APPLY-02).
- **Depends on:** GAP-HR-LEAVE-APPLY-04, GAP-HR-LEAVE-APPLY-05

### GAP-HR-LEAVE-APPLY-02  ·  HIGH  ·  confirmed  ·  theme ROLEGATE

- [x] **Status** — PR #1651 (merged, GAP-HR-SF-16): `leave/context-routes.ts` scoped, matching `/leave-allocations`' existing `resolveLeaveReadScope` pattern.
- **First-pass claim:** GET /leave-context takes any employeeId with only a role check (leave/context-routes.ts:10-15; no ownership scope, unlike /leave-allocations): any employee can enumerate colleagues' balances by UUID through the same call the form makes.
- **Verified evidence:** context-routes.ts:10-15 requireRole(ctx, ALL_ROLES) where ALL_ROLES includes manager and employee (line 7), parses any employeeId and calls employeeRepo.findById(q.employeeId, ctx.tenantId) with only a tenant filter; it returns the employee's name/employeeNo and every allocation (fy, totalDays, balanceDays) (21-49). No resolveLeaveReadScope call, unlike GET /leave-allocations (routes.ts:214-223) which uses resolveLeaveReadScope (routes.ts:158-171). 404 vs 200 also lets a caller test whether a UUID is an employee. Both /hr/leave/apply and /hr/leave/balance use this call.
- **Files to change:** `services/hrms-service/src/modules/leave/context-routes.ts`, `services/hrms-service/src/modules/leave/routes.ts`, `services/hrms-service/src/modules/leave/read-scope.ts (new)`, `services/hrms-service/src/modules/leave/__tests__/leave-context-scope.test.ts (new)`
- **Fix steps:**
  1. Move resolveNonHrEmployeeScope/resolveLeaveReadScope out of routes.ts into a new leave/read-scope.ts and export them; import in routes.ts and context-routes.ts.
  2. In the /v1/hrms/leave-context handler, before findById: const scope = await resolveLeaveReadScope(ctx, req, q.employeeId); if (scope !== undefined && !scope.includes(q.employeeId)) throw new HttpError(403,'FORBIDDEN', ...).
  3. Decide manager self-access: resolveNonHrEmployeeScope returns only direct reports for managers (routes.ts:152-158), so a manager could no longer read their own balance; include the actor's own employee id for the manager case in this route.
  4. Add a real-DB test modelled on manager-employee-read-scope-real-db.test.ts: employee A gets 403 for employee B, 200 for self; manager gets 200 for a report, 403 for a non-report; HR gets 200.

  - Manager token: direct report 200, other 403, self 200.

### GAP-HR-LEAVE-HISTORY-01  ·  MEDIUM  ·  partly  ·  theme FAILMASK (was ROLEGATE)

- [x] **Status** — PR #1733 (merged): real server-side pagination/ordering/total/statusCounts, replacing a fake meta.total = data.length.
- **First-pass claim:** Stats are not source-gated: while loading or after a failed fetch the tiles show real 0s (LeaveHistoryClient.tsx:162-169), and they count only the first 50 applications (limit=50, line 98) with no pager, so totals silently under-report for long histories.
- **Verified evidence:** Tiles render unconditionally (LeaveHistoryClient.tsx:162-170) from apps.length/filters; apps starts [] (59) so tiles show real 0s while loading (the loading flag only hides the table, 208-214) and after a failed fetch the catch (104) sets only source='error', leaving the previous employee's array in state so the tiles show stale counts above an error card. Line 98 sends limit=50, but the server ignores it for employee-scoped reads: routes.ts:314-323 uses getLeaveApplicationsByEmp -> repo.findLeaveAppsByEmp with fixed default limit 100 (repo.ts:51-55), no ORDER BY, no offset, and reports meta.total = data.length (routes.ts:323). So counts silently under-report beyond 100 rows (not 50), and which rows are dropped is arbitrary.
- **Files to change:** `apps/web/src/app/(app)/hr/leave/history/LeaveHistoryClient.tsx`, `services/hrms-service/src/modules/leave/routes.ts`, `services/hrms-service/src/modules/leave/repo.ts`, `services/hrms-service/src/modules/leave/queries.ts`
- **Fix steps:**
  1. Web: render tiles only when !loading && source==='api' && empId; otherwise show '—' (StatCard value string). Clear apps on employee change/fetch error (setApps([]) in catch).
  2. Backend: make findLeaveAppsByEmp honour limit/offset with ORDER BY created_at DESC and return a real total (count query); return meta.total accurately in routes.ts:323.
  3. Web: show pager or 'Showing N of M' and compute tile counts from a server aggregate (status counts) rather than the loaded page.
- **Acceptance:**
  - Test: while loading and on 500 the tiles show '—', never 0.
  - API test: employee with 120 applications returns total 120 and honours limit/offset newest first.
  - Switching employee never shows the previous employee's counts.
- **Needs:** web+backend  ·  **Effort:** M ~1-2d  ·  **Risk:** Low money risk; aggregate counts must respect the same read scope (resolveLeaveReadScope).

### GAP-HR-ONBOARDING-DETAIL-01  ·  HIGH  ·  confirmed  ·  theme DEADROUTE

- [x] **Status** — PR #1685 (merged): ChecklistWithActions wired to the existing PATCH .../complete endpoint. Pre-existing task-ownership verification gap on that endpoint honestly carried forward as a flagged, not silently fixed, issue.
- **First-pass claim:** Checklist is read-only: OnboardingChecklist supports a 'Mark done' button via onComplete but page.tsx never passes it, although PATCH /v1/hrms/onboarding-tasks/:taskId/complete exists (onboarding-routes.ts:122). HR cannot tick a task off from the joinee's own page — the tracker's progress and overdue counts can never move from the UI.
- **Verified evidence:** OnboardingChecklist (client component, _components/OnboardingChecklist.tsx:20,205-222) renders 'Mark done' only when onComplete is passed; [id]/page.tsx:262 renders <OnboardingChecklist steps={checklist} /> with no handler. PATCH /v1/hrms/onboarding-tasks/:taskId/complete exists (lifecycle/onboarding-routes.ts:122) and is applied asynchronously via publishF3Write (f3-consumer.ts:227), so UI must refresh after a delay. Note page.tsx is a server component and cannot pass a function prop; a client wrapper is needed.
- **Files to change:** `apps/web/src/app/(app)/hr/onboarding/[id]/page.tsx`, `apps/web/src/app/(app)/hr/onboarding/_components/ChecklistWithActions.tsx (new)`
- **Fix steps:**
  1. Create a 'use client' ChecklistWithActions wrapping OnboardingChecklist that implements onComplete(id) with fetch PATCH /api/proxy/v1/hrms/onboarding-tasks/{id}/complete.
  2. Use optimistic 'completed' state, roll back and show toHumanError on failure, then router.refresh() (writes are queue-async; poll or refresh once after ~1s).
  3. Replace <OnboardingChecklist steps={checklist}/> at page.tsx:262 with the wrapper.
- **Acceptance:**
  - Click Mark done: step shows completed, progress bar on refresh increments.
  - API 500 rolls the step back and shows an error.
- **Needs:** web  ·  **Effort:** S ~half day  ·  **Risk:** HR-only route; the API does not verify the task belongs to the page's employee, so do not rely on UI for authz.

### GAP-HR-ONBOARDING-DETAIL-02  ·  HIGH  ·  confirmed  ·  theme DEADROUTE

- [x] **Status** — PR #1716 (merged): verify/reject/mark-received wired to real actions, server-role-gated (requireRole HR_ROLES), cross-employee write isolation confirmed (tenantId+employeeId+docType scoped). Rescan follow-up: DocCard re-adopts the server status/file after a refresh (Verify/Reject now show in-session); DocumentsPanel polls the documents list after each write and refreshes once the committed status is visible (honest 'still processing' otherwise); the upload card now offers only PDF/JPG/PNG/DOCX and presigns under the 'attachment' category so image uploads no longer 400. Tests: DocumentUploadCard.test.tsx, DocumentsPanel.test.tsx. (W2 hr rescan: completed by #PRNUM)
- **First-pass claim:** Document upload does not register with HRMS: DocumentUploadCard presigns and PUTs the file (POST /admin/uploads/presign), sets local status 'uploaded' and calls onUploaded, which the page never wires — mark-received and verify/reject routes exist (onboarding-routes.ts:181-200) but are never called. After a refresh the document is 'pending' again and there is no way for HR to verify or reject.
- **Verified evidence:** [id]/page.tsx:288 renders <DocumentUploadCard documents={documents} /> without onUploaded. DocumentUploadCard.tsx:88-105 presigns via /api/proxy/v1/admin/uploads/presign, PUTs, sets local state and calls onUploaded?.(doc.id,key) (no-op). Routes PATCH .../mark-received and .../verify exist (onboarding-routes.ts:181-200; consumers f3-consumer.ts:246-300). Additionally hrms_onboarding_documents (lifecycle/schema.ts:221-234) has no column for the storage key, so even a wired mark-received records only status/receivedAt; the object key is lost and HR cannot open the file.
- **Files to change:** `apps/web/src/app/(app)/hr/onboarding/[id]/page.tsx`, `apps/web/src/app/(app)/hr/onboarding/_components/DocumentUploadCard.tsx`, `apps/web/src/app/(app)/hr/onboarding/_components/DocumentsPanel.tsx (new client wrapper)`, `services/hrms-service/src/modules/lifecycle/schema.ts`, `services/hrms-service migrations (new storage_key)`, `services/hrms-service/src/modules/lifecycle/f3-consumer.ts`, `services/hrms-service/src/modules/lifecycle/onboarding-routes.ts`
- **Fix steps:**
  1. Backend: add storage_key (and file name) to hrms_onboarding_documents; accept it in mark-received body (zod) and persist in f3-consumer __3; return it (as a short-lived download URL) in GET onboarding-documents.
  2. Web: create a client DocumentsPanel that passes onUploaded to call PATCH mark-received with {storageKey}, then router.refresh().
  3. Add Verify/Reject buttons for status 'uploaded' calling PATCH .../verify {status}; hide for non-HR roles.
  4. Add a 'View' link using the presigned download URL.
- **Acceptance:**
  - Upload a file, reload: document shows 'uploaded' not 'pending'.
  - HR clicks Verify: status 'verified', verifiedBy set; Reject shows 'rejected'.
  - HR can open the uploaded file.
- **Needs:** web+backend  ·  **Effort:** M ~1-2d  ·  **Risk:** PII documents (Aadhaar/PAN); storage links must be tenant-scoped and short-lived.
- **Depends on:** GAP-HR-ONBOARDING-DETAIL-03

### GAP-HR-ONBOARDING-DETAIL-05  ·  MEDIUM  ·  confirmed  ·  theme FAILMASK (was OTHER)

- **First-pass claim:** Designation and department are raw id fragments: buildSubtree sets designation = designationId.slice(0, 8) and department = departmentId.slice(0, 8) (services/hrms-service/src/modules/orgchart/queries.ts:19-20), so every node chip reads like 'a91f2c07' and search by designation or department can never match a real title.

OrgTreeNode.tsx:180 shows DesignationChip label={node.designation}, and search (OrgTreeNode.tsx:73-78) matches on those fragments. hrms_designations and hrms_departments tables exist (employee/schema.ts:8,27) but the org chart never reads them. Note queries.ts also uses employeeRepo.listByTenant(2000) and is cached via cache.listOrLoad.
- **Files to change:** `services/hrms-service/src/modules/orgchart/queries.ts`, `services/hrms-service/src/modules/employee/repo.ts (name lookups)`, `packages/schemas OrgChartSchema (if fields added)`
- **Fix steps:**

  2. In buildSubtree return designation: designationName ?? '—', department: departmentName ?? '—' (optionally also designationId/departmentId).
  3. Invalidate the org_chart cache when designations/departments change.
  4. Add test: node.designation equals designation title.
- **Acceptance:**
  - Org chart chip reads 'Under Secretary' not 'a91f2c07'.
  - Search 'Secretary' finds matching nodes.
- **Needs:** backend  ·  **Effort:** S ~half day  ·  **Risk:** Cache key must stay tenant-scoped; schema validation via sendValidated must accept fields.

### GAP-HR-ORG-CHART-02  ·  HIGH  ·  confirmed  ·  theme OTHER

- [x] **Status** — PR #1697 (merged): independently reviewed clean.
- **First-pass claim:** Stats are computed over the root list only: the API returns roots with nested children (orgchart/queries.ts:34-39) but page.tsx:20-23 does nodes.filter(children).length and new Set(nodes.map(department)).size, so 'Managers' and 'Departments' count top-level heads, not the whole tree; only 'Total Employees' recurses (countAll).
- **Verified evidence:** page.tsx:21-23: managers = nodes.filter(children.length>0).length and uniqueDepts = new Set(nodes.map(department)).size run over top-level nodes only; only totalCount uses recursive countAll (page.tsx:8-13). So Managers and Departments understate. Also `roots` (page.tsx:23) filters !reportsTo, and roots with a separated manager have reportsTo set (see ORG-CHART-05).
- **Files to change:** `apps/web/src/app/(app)/hr/org-chart/page.tsx`
- **Fix steps:**
  1. Add flatten(nodes) helper (recursive) and compute managers = flat.filter(has children).length, departments = new Set(flat.map(department)).size.
  2. Compute roots as nodes.length (the API returns roots).
  3. Unit-test with a 3-level tree.
- **Acceptance:**
  - Tree A(B(C),D): managers=2, total=4, departments per data.
- **Needs:** web  ·  **Effort:** XS <1h  ·  **Risk:** Low.
- **Depends on:** GAP-HR-ORG-CHART-01

### GAP-HR-OVERTIME-01  ·  HIGH  ·  confirmed  ·  theme WIRING

- [x] **Status** — PR #1707 (merged): identity resolved via resolveEmployeeForActor, no raw UUID. W2 rescan: a 404/409 on approve/reject now says the request was already decided and refreshes the list; a 202 says the decision is being applied; the dialogs are localised and no longer claim payroll disbursement; reject-reason-in-body, already-decided and role cases tested. (W2 hr rescan: completed by #PRNUM)
- **First-pass claim:** Subtitle 'Review and track… linked to payroll disbursement' and empty copy 'appear here for approval' imply an approval queue, but there are no approve/reject controls; PATCH …/approve|reject exist HR-only (attendance/routes.ts:296,323). Pending requests can only be actioned via the API.
- **Verified evidence:** overtime/page.tsx renders PageHeader (subtitle en.json overtime.subtitle 'Review and track employee overtime requests -- linked to payroll disbursement'), stat card 'Pending Approval', and empty copy 'Overtime requests submitted by employees will appear here for approval', but the DataTable (lines 81-91) has no action column and there is no other web caller of PATCH /v1/hrms/overtime-requests/:id/approve|reject (grep of apps/web/src shows only OvertimeClaimForm POST). The endpoints exist, HR_ROLES only (attendance/routes.ts:296 and 323), pre-check status=pending, return 202, reject accepts optional reason (max 500). So pending requests cannot be actioned from the UI. No link between overtime and payroll disbursement is visible in this page (claim is copy only).
- **Files to change:** `apps/web/src/app/(app)/hr/overtime/page.tsx`, `apps/web/src/app/(app)/hr/overtime/_components/OvertimeActions.tsx (new)`, `apps/web/src/messages/en.json`
- **Fix steps:**
  1. Add a client component OvertimeActions with Approve and Reject buttons per pending row (rendered only for HR roles from the session role list); Reject opens ds/ConfirmDialog with a reason textarea (max 500).
  2. Call PATCH /api/proxy/v1/hrms/overtime-requests/{id}/approve and /reject; treat 202 as accepted, show toast, then router.refresh() (async consumer, so poll or show 'processing').
  3. Extend DataTable columns in overtime/page.tsx with an actions cell; handle 404 'already decided' by refreshing.
  4. Remove 'linked to payroll disbursement' from the subtitle unless the payroll link is confirmed (cannot verify payroll consumption from this snapshot).
- **Acceptance:**
  - Component test: pending row shows Approve/Reject for hr_admin, none for employee/manager.
  - Reject requires a reason in the dialog and sends it in the body.
  - Approving an already decided request shows a friendly message and refreshes the list.
- **Needs:** web  ·  **Effort:** M ~1-2d  ·  **Risk:** Approval action on pay-related data: use ConfirmDialog, do not allow the requester to approve their own request (maker != checker is not enforced by the backend today: routes.ts:296-323 has no self-approval check).
- **Depends on:** GAP-HR-OVERTIME-02, GAP-HR-OVERTIME-05

### GAP-HR-PAY-MATRIX-01  ·  HIGH  ·  partly  ·  theme PAYROLL-DATA (was MONEY)

- [x] **Status** — PR #1710 (merged): matrix labeled as computed/not-official until PAY_MATRIX_OFFICIAL=true. official flag now returned on GET.
- **First-pass claim:** Page is labelled '7th CPC Pay Matrix … (eHRMS reference)' but pay-matrix/routes.ts:11–37 does not hold the official matrix: it seeds cell 1 per level and multiplies by 1.03 rounded up to the next ₹100, which does not reproduce the notified cell values or per-level cell counts — a payroll reference showing computed figures as statutory.
- **Verified evidence:** pay-matrix/routes.ts:11-37 confirmed: ENTRY_PAY_PAISE seeds cell 1 per level (paise), CELL_COUNT sets cells (40 for levels 1-12, then 19,18,13,9,1,1), and buildPayMatrix multiplies by 1.03 and rounds UP to the next Rs 100 (Math.ceil(cur*1.03/10000)*10000). The file's own doc comment calls the result 'generated', though the page header (en.json payMatrix.subtitle) says 'per the 7th CPC (eHRMS reference)' and the values are shown with no 'illustrative' marker. Money is correctly held in paise. I cannot verify the notified table (not in the snapshot); from public knowledge of the 7th CPC matrix (e.g. Level 1: 18,000 -> 18,500 -> 19,100) rounding-up produces 18,600 for cell 2, so values likely differ from official ones, but that comparison needs the official gazette table. Note the same PAY_MATRIX drives POST /pay-matrix/annual-increment (routes.ts ~150-230), which writes basicMinor to employees and service book, so the risk extends beyond display.
- **Files to change:** `services/hrms-service/src/modules/pay-matrix/routes.ts (or a new pay-matrix/data/cpc7.json + loader)`, `apps/web/src/app/(app)/hr/pay-matrix/page.tsx`, `apps/web/src/messages/en.json`
- **Fix steps:**
  1. Obtain the notified 7th CPC matrix (all 18 levels x cells) from the source document and store as data (JSON/DB seed table hrms_pay_matrix) in paise; replace buildPayMatrix with the table.
  2. Add a unit test comparing spot cells (level 1 cell 1-5, level 10 cell 1, level 18) with the notified values, and a test that cell counts equal the notification.
  3. Until fixed: mark the page and the increment dry-run response as 'computed / not official' and block the non-dry-run annual increment.
  4. Reuse the same table in /pay-matrix/lookup and annual-increment.
- **Acceptance:**
  - Test: official values for the sample cells match exactly.

With raw rows the table columns employee/department/fromGrade/toGrade/orderNo are blank (keys absent; orderRef vs orderNo) and PromotionCard falls back to the UUID (PromotionCard.tsx:72-74). Extra: the raw row contains a bigint newBasicMinor and I found no BigInt JSON serializer in hrms-service, so the raw endpoint may 500 for rows with a non-null value (cannot verify runtime). ### GAP-HR-PROMOTION-02  ·  HIGH  ·  partly  ·  theme STATUS

- [x] **Status** — PR #1705 (merged): same stepper rework as PROMOTION-01.
- **First-pass claim:** Status vocabulary does not match the backend: the wizard creates `pending_approval` and the eOffice consumer moves it to `pending_effective` or `cancelled` (promotion-eoffice-consumer.ts:69,97), but the page counts pending/dept_approved/hr_approved/finance_approved/signed (page.tsx:41–44) and PromotionCard prints the raw code as the label (PromotionCard.tsx:69); every real promotion is in Total only and the 4-step 'Dept Head→HR→Finance→Signed' chain shows nothing reached.
- **Verified evidence:** The status vocabulary mismatch is real, but overstated. Backend statuses: 'pending' (default in lifecycle/schema.ts:49 and direct POST route), 'pending_approval' (submit-approval), then promotion-eoffice-consumer.ts:68-97 moves pending_approval -> pending_effective, then -> completed when effective date is due (or cancelled on reject). page.tsx:39-42 counts approved = approved|signed|completed|finance_approved, pending = ['pending'], inApproval = dept_approved|hr_approved, completed = signed|completed. So 'completed' promotions ARE counted (Approved/Signed and Signed&Issued); pending_approval, pending_effective and cancelled fall only in Total. PromotionCard.tsx:35-44 STATUS_LABEL_KEYS lacks pending_approval, pending_effective; the raw code is printed (line 69) for those, and the 4-step chain (CHAIN, lines 46-51) never advances for them (chainIndex returns -1). 'Initiated' also only counts 'pending'. Line refs in the observation are off by ~2 (page.tsx:39-42).
- **Files to change:** `apps/web/src/app/(app)/hr/promotion/page.tsx`, `apps/web/src/app/(app)/hr/promotion/_components/PromotionCard.tsx`, `apps/web/src/app/_components/ds/StatusPill.tsx`, `apps/web/src/messages/en.json`
- **Fix steps:**
  1. Define one exported PROMOTION_STATUS map (pending, pending_approval, pending_effective, completed, cancelled + legacy dept/hr/finance/signed) with label key, StatusPill tone and stage.
  2. Use it in page.tsx counters: Initiated = pending|pending_approval; In approval/Awaiting effective date = pending_effective; Completed = completed|signed; Cancelled separate.
  3. Add en.json labels statusPendingApproval ('Awaiting eOffice approval'), statusPendingEffective ('Approved - effective on date').
  4. Add tones for pending_approval (warn), pending_effective (info), cancelled (bad/mut) to StatusPill STATUS_MAP.
  5. Replace the Dept/HR/Finance/Signed chain (see GAP-HR-PROMOTION-04).
- **Acceptance:**
  - Unit test: each backend status maps to a label and tone; counters sum with cancelled to Total.
  - A pending_approval row shows 'Awaiting eOffice approval', not the raw code.
- **Needs:** web  ·  **Effort:** S ~half day  ·  **Risk:** Low; be careful to keep legacy statuses so old rows still render.
- **Depends on:** GAP-HR-PROMOTION-04

### GAP-HR-RTI-01  ·  HIGH  ·  confirmed  ·  theme STATUS (was DATEFMT)

- [x] **Status** — PR #1690 (merged): independently reviewed clean.
- **First-pass claim:** SLA label is wrong for answered requests: only status "closed" gets "Closed" (page.tsx:62); a "responded" or "appealed" request past its due date has overdue=false (open = filed|assigned only, rti/routes.ts:15) so it prints a negative "-32 days left" through the ICU plural (page.tsx:64), which reads as nonsense to the CPIO.
- **Verified evidence:** apps/web/src/app/(app)/hr/rti/page.tsx:59-67: only status==='closed' gets slaClosed; else overdue ? slaOverdueByDays : slaDueInDays(daysToDue). Backend withSla (services/hrms-service/src/modules/rti/routes.ts:15-21) sets overdue only for status filed|assigned, and daysToDue = due - today with no clamp, so a 'responded' or 'appealed' row past its due date has overdue=false and daysToDue<0 -> en.json:4076 ICU renders '-32 days left' (=0 'Due today', one, other; -1 gives '-1 day left'). Theme DATEFMT is wrong.

- **Fix steps:**

  2. Never pass a negative days value to slaDueInDays; guard with Math.max(0, ...) as a last resort.
  3. Add keys to en.json and hi.json next to l.4074-4076.
  4. Product decision: whether an appealed request shows a separate appeal deadline (RTI s.19 first-appeal clock); backend currently has none.
- **Acceptance:**
  - Unit test: status 'responded', dueDate 32 days ago -> label 'Responded', not '-32 days left'.
  - Status 'assigned' 2 days overdue still shows '2 days overdue'.
- **Needs:** web  ·  **Effort:** XS <1h  ·  **Risk:** Low; statutory deadline display for CPIO/PIO, keep overdue logic for open requests unchanged.

- **Files to change:** `apps/web/src/app/(app)/hr/rti/page.tsx`, `apps/web/src/app/(app)/hr/rti/[id]/page.tsx (new)`, `apps/web/src/app/(app)/hr/rti/_components/FileRtiAction.tsx (new)`, `apps/web/src/app/(app)/hr/rti/_components/RtiActions.tsx (new)`, `apps/web/src/messages/en.json`, `apps/web/src/messages/hi.json`

  4. Surface 409 INVALID_STATE and 403 SEGREGATION_OF_DUTIES messages via toHumanError.
  5. Add tests for each form's validation.
- **Acceptance:**

### GAP-HR-RTI-06  ·  LOW  ·  partly  ·  theme TIMEZONE (was DATEFMT)

- [x] **Status** — PR #1690 (merged): independently reviewed clean.
- **First-pass claim:** "Overdue" stat card counts the overdue flag computed server-side at request time in UTC (withSla uses toISOString), so at the IST day boundary the count can be one day out.
- **Verified evidence:** services/hrms-service/src/modules/rti/routes.ts:16 `today = new Date().toISOString().slice(0,10)` is the UTC date. IST is UTC+5:30, so from 00:00 to 05:30 IST the server 'today' is still yesterday: overdue flips 5.5 hours late and daysToDue is one higher. It is per-request, and only affects that window each day. The web page just counts i.overdue (apps/web/src/app/(app)/hr/rti/page.tsx:48).
- **Files to change:** `services/hrms-service/src/modules/rti/routes.ts`
- **Fix steps:**
  1. Compute today with new Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-CA',{timeZone:'Asia/Kolkata'}).format(new Date()) (or a shared helper in shared/) and use it in withSla.
  2. Add unit test with a fake clock at 2026-09-29T19:00Z (00:30 IST 30 Sep).
- **Acceptance:**
  - At 00:30 IST on due date+1, the request is overdue=true.
  - Existing withSla tests still pass.
- **Needs:** backend  ·  **Effort:** XS <1h  ·  **Risk:** Low; deadline calculation used for statutory tracking.

### GAP-HR-SERVICE-BOOK-01  ·  HIGH  ·  partly  ·  theme ATTESTATION (was PII)

- **First-pass claim:** Service book is a legal service record, yet there is no attestation display, no entry status and no print/PDF: the API sends status attested|recorded (m7-list-routes.ts:156) and a PDF route exists (services/hrms-service/src/modules/service-book/pdf-routes.ts:42), but the table drops status and offers no export. Unattested entries look identical to attested ones.
- **Verified evidence:** Confirmed: API sends status 'attested'|'recorded' (services/hrms-service/src/modules/lifecycle/m7-list-routes.ts:138) and ServiceEntry carries status (ServiceBookView.tsx:23), but COLUMNS (l.111) and the row cells (l.209-253) never render it; no print/export control exists. A PDF route exists (services/hrms-service/src/modules/service-book/pdf-routes.ts:36) but (a) it is per-employee, (b) it returns text/html, not a PDF, (c) its table (l.42) omits attested status, and (d) unlike the JSON route it applies no manager department scoping (READER_ROLES incl. manager, pdf-routes.ts:38) - a security gap. Attest endpoint is POST /v1/hrms/service-book/entries/:entryId/attest (routes.ts:83) with no UI. Theme PII is wrong.

- **Fix steps:**

  2. Add a filter option 'Unattested only' and a KPI card counting recorded entries.
  3. When empId is set, add a 'Print service book' link to /api/v1/hrms/employees/{empId}/service-book/pdf (new tab).
  4. Backend: add attested/attestedAt columns to the PDF rows, apply the same dept scoping as routes.ts:28-37 (extract a shared assertCanReadEmployee), and either render a real PDF or rename the route/content-type honestly.
  5. Optionally add attest action for HR_ROLES (confirm dialog, calls attest endpoint) with pending state.
- **Acceptance:**

  - Manager from another department gets 403 on the pdf route.
  - Print link opens the employee's document containing an Attested column.
- **Needs:** web+backend  ·  **Effort:** M ~1-2d  ·  **Risk:** Legal service record; PDF scoping bug is a data-exposure risk (manager can enumerate employees) and should be fixed regardless.

- **First-pass claim:** Employee self-scope uses ctx.actorId as employeeId (attendance/routes.ts:186-188 effectiveEmpId = ctx.actorId) while requests are stored by hrms_employees.id from getMyProfile — a plain employee will see an empty list of their own requests (same id-space bug GeoCheckInCard.tsx:26-36 documents for geo-history).
- **Verified evidence:** attendance/routes.ts:186-188 sets effectiveEmpId = ctx.actorId for non-HR/manager callers and filters hrmsShiftChangeRequests.employeeId by it. The page (shift-requests/page.tsx:64-67) prefills the form with getMyProfile().id (an hrms_employees.id, loaders.ts:1151-1163) and POST (routes.ts:447-462) stores body.employeeId. Employee-role list therefore matches nothing. Worse: the POST IDOR guard at routes.ts:460 (body.employeeId !== ctx.actorId) 403s the same employee's own submit, and the self-approval guards (routes.ts:485,511 employeeId === ctx.actorId) never trigger, so an HR/manager who is also an employee could approve their own request. GeoCheckInCard.tsx:26-36 documents the same id-space split; resolveEmployeeForActor (employee/actor-link.ts) is the intended resolver.
- **Files to change:** `services/hrms-service/src/modules/attendance/routes.ts`, `services/hrms-service/src/modules/attendance/__tests__/shift-requests-self-scope.test.ts`
- **Fix steps:**
  1. In GET /v1/hrms/shift-requests, when !isHrOrManager call resolveEmployeeForActor(ctx.tenantId, ctx.actorId); if null return {data:[]}, else use actorEmp.id as effectiveEmpId.
  2. In POST /v1/hrms/shift-requests replace body.employeeId !== ctx.actorId with a comparison against the resolved actorEmp.id for non-HR actors.
  3. In PATCH approve and reject, resolve the actor's employee id once and compare existing[0].employeeId to it (keep the ctx.actorId compare only as a fallback for the same value).
  4. Add tests: employee lists own request, employee creates for self (202), employee creates for other (403), HR who owns the request cannot approve it.
- **Acceptance:**
  - Test: employee JWT (actorId != employee.id, userRef linked) submits then GET returns exactly that row.
  - Test: POST with another employee's id returns 403.
  - Manual: log in as plain employee at /hr/shift-requests, submit a request; it appears in the list after refresh.
- **Needs:** backend  ·  **Effort:** S ~half day  ·  **Risk:** Approval/self-approval control: fixing the id space changes who can approve; cover with tests. Related wfh/overtime routes at routes.ts:226,373,398,424 share the same actorId comparison.

- [x] **Status** — PR #1706 (merged): hex replaced with CSS vars, decorative dots aria-hidden, one role=img aria-label summary per row.

- **Verified evidence:** social/routes.ts:222-262: GET /v1/hrms/social/feed calls resolveContext but no requireRole (any authenticated tenant user, including employees) and returns each employee with status='confirmed' whose DOB month/day is today: name, department, designation (no year, no consent/opt-out column queried). The page prints them (page.tsx:104-113). Layout admits all listed roles. Birthday cut is by server-local date (new Date(), not IST). No birthday cap, so busy days also crowd the slice(0,30).

  3. Compute today in Asia/Kolkata (e.g. (NOW() AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Kolkata')::date).

  3. Add a unit test with fillPercentage "87.5" and 0.

### GAP-HR-SUCCESSION-01  ·  HIGH  ·  confirmed  ·  theme FABRICATED

- [x] **Status** — PR #1703 (merged): synthesise() placeholder-name generator deleted; real successors from a joined succession_nominees/hrms_employees query.
- **First-pass claim:** When the API sends no `successors` (it never does: gap-features/routes.ts:268 returns only role_ref, department_id, nominee_count, ready_now), page.tsx:79–99 fabricates placeholder people ('Nominee 1…n') with invented ids and splits non-ready counts half '1–2 Years' / half '3–5 Years' — fictional readiness data presented as a real pipeline.

The API has no such split (readiness is now/1yr/2yr/3yr per nominee), so the cards show fabricated names and readiness.

- **Fix steps:**

  2. Backend: extend GET /v1/hrms/succession/pipeline (or add /succession/plans/:id/nominees) to return per-nominee rows {employeeId, fullName, readiness, developmentPlan} joined from employee.succession_nominees + hrms_employees.
  3. Map API readiness now/1yr/2yr/3yr to the UI Readiness union in one mapper (see SUCCESSION-03).
  4. When a plan has nominee_count>0 but no nominee detail, render counts ('3 nominees, 1 ready now') instead of person rows; SuccessionPlanCard shows the existing noSuccessorsWarning only when nominee_count===0.
  5. Remove nomineeName key from all five src/messages/*.json.
- **Acceptance:**
  - Component test: pipeline row {nominee_count:3, ready_now:1} with no successors renders no 'Nominee N' text and no invented ids.
  - Component test: row with real successors renders their names and mapped readiness.

- **First-pass claim:** page.tsx:46–51 defines `render: (r) => r.rating.toFixed(1)` and passes the columns to DataTable, a "use client" component (DataTable.tsx:1) whose own comment says render 'cannot be passed from Server Components' (DataTable.tsx:44); this server page will throw on render for every non-empty response and land on error.tsx.
- **Verified evidence:** apps/web/src/app/(app)/hr/training/feedback/page.tsx is a server component (no 'use client', uses getTranslations/getSessionRoles) and builds `columns` with `render: (r) => r.rating.toFixed(1)` (line ~47), passed to DataTable which is 'use client' (DataTable.tsx:1) and documents render as client-only (DataTable.tsx:44-45). Next 14 rejects function props crossing the RSC boundary, so the page errors whenever the DataTable branch renders, i.e. every non-error load INCLUDING empty results (columns are serialised regardless of rows), not only non-empty. Same pattern exists in other server pages (e.g. hr/holidays/page.tsx:91), so this is systemic. Cannot run the app here; conclusion is from the documented RSC rule.
- **Files to change:** `apps/web/src/app/(app)/hr/training/feedback/page.tsx`, `services/hrms-service/src/modules/training/routes.ts`
- **Fix steps:**
  1. Remove `render` from the rating column; in mapResponse produce a display string field (e.g. ratingLabel) and use key 'ratingLabel', or use a server-safe cellType.
  2. Better: keep numeric `score` for sorting and add a small 'use client' wrapper component (FeedbackTable.tsx) that owns the columns with render if custom cells are needed.
  3. Add a lint/test guard: no `render:` in server page.tsx passed to DataTable.
  4. Apply the same fix to the other server pages that pass render (grep `render:` in page.tsx without 'use client').
- **Acceptance:**
  - Render test of the page module (async server component) with mocked fetchJson returning 2 rows: no 'Functions cannot be passed directly to Client Components' error.
  - Manual: /hr/training/feedback with an HR login loads instead of error.tsx.
- **Needs:** web  ·  **Effort:** XS <1h  ·  **Risk:** Low; page currently errors so any working render is an improvement.

## /hr/training/new  —  `hr/training-new.html`

- **Source:** `apps/web/src/app/(app)/hr/training/new/page.tsx`

### GAP-HR-TRAINING-NEW-01  ·  HIGH  ·  confirmed  ·  theme WIRING (was VALIDATION)

- [x] **Status** — PR #1719 (merged): unmount-safe redirect (was a bare setTimeout leak) + stacked caching bug fixed (Next fetch cache + hrms-service in-process cache, both confirmed root causes). W2 hr rescan: the form no longer redirects on a fixed 1.5 s timer. After the 202 it reads the accepted {id}, shows "Submitted" (shared AcceptedNotice), polls the programmes list (limit=500, bounded to 5 attempts with backoff, via useAcceptedWrite) and moves to /hr/training only once the id is present; if the poll runs out it shows a non-error "still processing" notice with a link to /hr/training?created=<id>, and the list shows a pending notice (PendingProgramNotice with a real Refresh) while that id is absent. Fields and submit stay locked after the 202 (no duplicate create) and the poll is cancelled on unmount. A consumer failure cannot be told apart from a slow consumer because no command-status endpoint exists (SF-15 notes building one is out of scope), so both end in the same honest "still processing" notice. Tests: poll finds the id on the 2nd attempt -> push; never found -> notice + created link + no redirect; unmount stops polling; list ?created= pending notice. (W2 hr rescan: completed by #PRNUM)
- **First-pass claim:** POST /trainings only queues a command and returns 202 accepted (commands.ts:12–20), yet the form reports 'Training program created successfully.' and redirects after 1.5 s (NewTrainingForm.tsx:70–72); the 300 s cached list (training-programs, revalidate 300) may not show it, and a consumer failure is never surfaced.
- **Verified evidence:** services/hrms-service/src/modules/training/routes.ts:73-78 POST /v1/hrms/trainings uses sendAccepted() and commands.ts:12-20 only publishes COMMANDS.trainingCreate and returns {id,status:'accepted',correlationId} (202 inferred from sendAccepted; the schemas package is not in this snapshot). Row is inserted later by consumer.ts:11-23. apps/web/src/app/(app)/hr/training/new/NewTrainingForm.tsx:63-72 treats res.ok as success: message 'Training program created successfully.' and router.push after 1500 ms. List loader getTrainingPrograms uses revalidateSeconds:300 (loaders.ts:2365) plus the service cache.listOrLoad (queries.ts:15), so the new row may be missing on redirect; consumer failure is never reported.
- **Files to change:** `apps/web/src/app/(app)/hr/training/new/NewTrainingForm.tsx`, `apps/web/src/app/_data/loaders.ts`, `apps/web/src/app/(app)/hr/training/page.tsx`
- **Fix steps:**
  1. Change success copy to 'Submitted - the programme will appear in the list shortly'.
  2. Read the accepted body {id}; after redirect, poll GET /api/proxy/v1/hrms/training-programs (few attempts, ~1s apart) until id appears, then router.refresh(); on timeout show a non-error 'still processing' notice with link.
  3. Expose a cache-busting path: after success call a server action/route that revalidates the 'hr.training' fetch tag (check apiClient for tag support) and add `?created=<id>` so the list can show a pending row.
  4. Disable submit while submitting (already disabled) and also after success to prevent duplicate creates.
  5. Replace setTimeout redirect with a cleanup-safe effect.
- **Acceptance:**
  - Test: mock 202 -> UI shows 'Submitted' wording, not 'created successfully'.
  - Test: poll finds id on 2nd attempt -> redirect; never finds -> notice shown.
  - Manual: create programme; it appears in /hr/training within 5 s without waiting 300 s.
- **Needs:** web  ·  **Effort:** S ~half day  ·  **Risk:** Duplicate-create risk if users resubmit while unsure; keep button disabled after 202.

### GAP-HR-TRAINING-NEW-03  ·  MEDIUM  ·  partly  ·  theme VALIDATION (was CAP)

- [x] **Status** — PR #1719 (merged): maxParticipants validation + non-blocking past-date warning, both with passing tests for the exact acceptance scenarios. W2 hr rescan: per-field errors are now i18n messages (required, too long with its limit, valid date, "Enter a whole number, 1 or more.") in en and hi, built from the trainingNew namespace, instead of bare zod tokens; the local IST helper is replaced by todayIST(). - [x] **Status** — PR #1714 (merged): date format fixed.
- **First-pass claim:** from_date/to_date are printed raw (page.tsx:40-41); node-pg returns DATE columns as JS Dates serialised as ISO timestamps, so users may see '2026-10-03T00:00:00.000Z' or a shifted day. No formatIndianDate.

Whether a DATE arrives as 'YYYY-MM-DD' or as a JS Date serialised to '...T00:00:00.000Z' depends on the postgres-js type config in packages/db, which is not in the snapshot (cannot verify); postgres-js defaults to Date objects. Note the observation names node-pg but the adapter is postgres-js (shared/db.ts:99-115). Either way the page never formats; formatIndianDate (lib/formatters.ts:2-7) exists but yields dd/mm/yyyy with no timeZone option, not 'dd Mon yyyy', and new Date('YYYY-MM-DD') is UTC so in a server with negative TZ offset the day could shift.

- **First-pass claim:** DPDP: named public servants and allegation wording for major proceedings, including cases that ended "dropped" (exonerated / discontinued), are visible in a searchable table to every hr_officer (page.tsx:76-88). A dropped case still shows the allegation indefinitely; no retention rule, masking or read audit.
- **Verified evidence:** vigilance/page.tsx:13,44-48 gate the page to hr_admin/hr_officer/super_admin (same as GET /v1/hrms/vigilance, gap-features/routes.ts:679-697). The table (page.tsx:76-89) shows employee, department, charge summary (allegation text) and status for every proceeding_type='major' case including 'dropped' and 'closed' (backend WHERE at :692 has no status/age filter); no masking, reveal, reason capture or read audit exists in the page or in that route (no audit call in the handler; audit only appears as comments elsewhere in the file). No retention/purge rule is visible in the snapshot (cannot verify). This is a real DPDP data-minimisation and purpose-limitation gap, severity depends on policy.

  3. Web: create a shared <Masked> component; render charges as a masked value with click-to-reveal that logs an access event; default filter to hide 'dropped'.

## /hr/wfh  —  `hr/wfh.html`

- **Source:** `apps/web/src/app/(app)/hr/wfh/page.tsx`
- **Design reference:** `redesign/hr/wfh.html`

### GAP-HR-WFH-01  ·  HIGH  ·  confirmed  ·  theme ELIGIBILITY (was VALIDATION)

- [~] **Status** — PARTIAL, owner decision pending. Done in the rescan: the weekly cap now counts DAYS (union of pending/approved ranges per ISO week plus the new request, de-duplicated), so a single Mon-Fri request or a request stacked on a multi-day one is refused 422 WEEKLY_WFH_CAP_REACHED, GET /wfh-eligibility reports days used, impossible calendar dates are 400 not 500, GAZETTED_NOT_ELIGIBLE / WEEKLY_WFH_CAP_REACHED have en+hi catalogue copy, and the page no longer second-guesses the server's count. The request form applies the server's this-week count only when the chosen dates touch that week (GET /wfh-eligibility also returns weekStart/weekEnd), so a full current week no longer stops someone filing for next week; the server still re-checks every touched week on submit. STILL OPEN (owner): (1) treating `hrms_designations.level` as the GoI pay level is an unverified assumption (default: Level 10+ excluded, per-tenant policy `wfh_eligibility`); (2) the cap counts calendar days, weekends and holidays included, the only reading that never loosens the cap on a 6-day-week tenant, but a Fri-Mon request (2 working days) is refused. Questions: is designation.level the authoritative pay level for WFH, and should weekly-offs / gazetted holidays be excluded from the 2-day count? (was: PR #1826 (merged))
- **First-pass claim:** DoPT eligibility is not enforced anywhere: the page renders WFHRequestForm without payLevel or weeklyWfhCount (page.tsx:105) so the gazetted (Level > 10) and 2-days-per-week guards never fire, and POST /wfh-requests validates only dates (attendance/routes.ts:360-372). Every user permanently sees 'Pay level could not be verified…' (WFHRequestForm.tsx: payLevelUnknown).
- **Verified evidence:** wfh/page.tsx:105 renders <WFHRequestForm employeeId=... redirectHref=.../> with no payLevel or weeklyWfhCount, so in WFHRequestForm.tsx isGazetted (:96) and weeklyCapReached (:97) are always false and payLevelUnknown (:98) is always true, showing the 'payLevelWarning' banner (:168-176) permanently. Backend POST /v1/hrms/wfh-requests (attendance/routes.ts:360-378) validates only employeeId, dates (toDate >= fromDate), reason and the IDOR guard; the consumer inserts unconditionally (attendance/f3-consumer.ts:193-200). No pay-level source is identifiable: hrms_employees has no pay-level column and hrms_designations only has `level` and `pay_grade` (employee/schema.ts:27-35); whether `level` maps to GoI pay level cannot be verified. There is no endpoint that counts approved WFH days per ISO week.
- **Files to change:** `services/hrms-service/src/modules/attendance/routes.ts`, `apps/web/src/app/(app)/hr/wfh/page.tsx`, `apps/web/src/app/(app)/hr/_components/WFHRequestForm.tsx`
- **Fix steps:**
  1. Decision: define the authoritative pay-level source (designation.level? pay-matrix?) and whether the 2-days/week cap counts pending + approved.
  2. Backend: in POST wfh-requests (after the zod parse) resolve the employee's pay level and reject gazetted (> 10) with a 422 code; count existing pending/approved days in the same ISO week(s) overlapping the range and reject if > 2; return machine-readable error codes.
  3. Add a read endpoint (or extend the list) giving the caller's weekly count so the page can pass weeklyWfhCount.
  4. Web: page.tsx fetches those values and passes payLevel/weeklyWfhCount into WFHRequestForm; hide the pay-level warning when known.
  5. Map the new error codes in useFormError.
- **Acceptance:**
  - Route test: gazetted employee POST -> 422; third WFH day in the same ISO week -> 422; two days allowed.
  - Component test: with payLevel=12 the form shows the gazetted error and submit is disabled.
  - Manual: non-gazetted user sees no warning banner.
- **Needs:** decision  ·  **Effort:** M ~1-2d  ·  **Risk:** Medium. Policy enforcement affects who may work remotely; wrong pay-level mapping would wrongly block or allow employees.
- **Depends on:** GAP-HR-WFH-02

### GAP-HR-WFH-02  ·  HIGH  ·  confirmed  ·  theme ROLEGATE

- [x] **Status** — PR #1649 (merged, GAP-HR-SF-10): actorId-vs-hrms_employees.id mismatch fixed; self-service and the inert self-approval guard fixed together. Rescan: the form is shown only to the roles the backend POST allows (new WFH_REQUEST_FILER_ROLES = hr_admin, hr_officer, super_admin, employee); a manager-only session sees an explanation and keeps Approve/Reject; a manager who is also an employee files for themselves only (no roster picker, which could only 403); route test: manager-only token POST -> 403. Decision taken conservatively: managers stay unable to file on behalf of reports (no new access granted). Owner question if wanted: may managers file WFH for direct reports (would need a reporting-line check)? (W2 hr rescan: completed by #PRNUM)

The IDOR guard at :369-372 compares body.employeeId with ctx.actorId; employee/actor-link.ts and medical/routes.ts:28-40 state actorId is the JWT subject and a different id space from hrms_employees.id (linked through userRef). Caveat: a manager JWT that also carries the 'employee' role would pass the role check.

### GAP-HR-WFH-06  ·  LOW  ·  confirmed  ·  theme VALIDATION (was DATEFMT)

- [~] **Status** — PARTIAL, owner decision pending. Done: IST-correct min (todayIST), all four stat cards pass null on error and a page test now asserts every card shows the dash on a failed load. STILL OPEN (owner): the back-dating policy is not decided, so the server accepts any fromDate (the `min` is a client-side hint only) and no server rule was invented. Question: may WFH be recorded retrospectively; if so by whom (employee or HR only) and up to how many days? (was: PR #1739 (merged): IST-correct date min; stats null not "—".)
- **First-pass claim:** From date min = today (WFHRequestForm.tsx) blocks recording a WFH day retrospectively; stats use '—' strings while sibling pages pass null.
- **Verified evidence:** WFHRequestForm.tsx:241 sets min={new Date().toISOString().split('T')[0]} on From date (and :260 min={fromDate || same} on To date), blocking past dates in the browser; toISOString is the UTC date so between 00:00 and 05:30 IST 'today' is yesterday's date. The backend does not enforce a lower bound (attendance/routes.ts:360-372), so the restriction is client-only; whether retrospective WFH is permitted is a policy question. Stats: wfh/page.tsx:93-96 pass the string '-' (em dash) on error whereas travel/page.tsx:56-59 and transfer/page.tsx:66-71 pass null to StatCard.

- **Fix steps:**
  1. Decision: allow back-dating (e.g. up to N days, HR only)? If yes, compute min from IST today minus N days; if no, keep min but compute IST today via Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-CA',{timeZone:'Asia/Kolkata'}).
  2. Add the same rule server-side in POST so the policy is enforced (see WFH-01).
  3. Change the four StatCard values to `errored ? null : n` to match sibling pages.
- **Acceptance:**

  - Component test: errored state passes null to StatCard.

- **Needs:** decision  ·  **Effort:** XS <1h  ·  **Risk:** Low; policy-dependent.

## Refuted by deep pass — do NOT implement

### GAP-HR-DEPUTATION-07 · /hr/deputation
- **First-pass claim:** Period is a backend-computed "36 mo" string (m7-list-routes.ts:164) — sorts alphabetically in the sortable DataTable, not numerically.
- **Why refuted:** Period is a backend string like '36 mo' (m7-list-routes.ts:21-31), but DataTable.compareValues (ds/DataTable.tsx:159-170) falls back to String.localeCompare(..., {numeric:true}), which orders '4 mo' before '36 mo'. Not alphabetical. Residual (not the claim): months use a 30-day approximation (:22) and '—' rows sort as text.

### GAP-HR-WORKFORCE-05 · /hr/workforce
- **First-pass claim:** DPDP: officer-level retirement date implies date of birth (retirement = DOB + 60 years, routes.ts:126); RetirementRow declares dateOfBirth (page.tsx:7). Visible to manager and finance_officer, who can see all departments, not just their reports.
- **Why refuted:** Not true of current code. retirement-forecast (routes.ts:115-157) returns only aggregates (period, retiring_count) — no names, DOB or per-officer dates; headcount is department counts. RetirementRow.dateOfBirth (page.tsx:7) is declared but never rendered (rtCols 50-56 exclude it) and no data feeds it. READER_ROLES (routes.ts:19) does include manager and finance_officer with tenant-wide scope, but they receive counts only. Risk becomes real only if WORKFORCE-01 is fixed by adding officer-level rows: then DOB derivable from retirement date (+60y) would need role-limited access and audit. Also web /hr layout HR_ROLES does not list finance_officer, so that role is redirected before this page.

### GAP-HR-WORKFORCE-CONTRACTUAL-02 · /hr/workforce/contractual

No change needed. Recommend deleting the redirect stub only if no bookmarks.
